To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Handover for Inês: border-revenues launch, Thursday 26 November

Inês,

I am very sorry to leave you with this mess, particularly with the figure 3 correction appearing only this afternoon. You should have been handed a clean launch, not a corrected report alongside slides and a press release that still contain the old number.

I also want to be completely clear about two things. First, the EUR 2.1 billion mistake is mine, not yours. If anyone asks, please say so. Second, I trust you completely to lead this launch. You know the paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself. You do not need to wait for my permission on any of the decisions below.

My father is ill, I am with my family. I am taking the train tonight and I do not yet know how long I will be away. You can call me, but after 09:00 tomorrow, Tuesday 24 November, I might not pick up. If I do not answer, make the decision that needs making and leave me a message; please do not let the launch stall while you wait for me.

Please work through things in this order.

1. Correct the public materials first

The corrected source of truth is PDF v7 on the drive. Pages 3, 14 and 15 have been corrected there.

The problem is that figure 3 and the summary used the 2030 revenue estimate from the old run, without the free-allocation phase-out applied. The correct 2030 LDC-relevant revenue figure is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The paper’s conclusion does not change, but the headline number does.

Two outputs are still wrong:

- Deck v4: correct slides 6 and 9. Slide 9 contains the revenue chart. Use PDF v7 as the reference, check the speaker notes as well, and search the finished deck for any remaining instance of “2.1”. Save a clearly marked new version so that nobody accidentally presents v4.
- The embargoed press release: Hanna sent this to our 34 Brussels contacts on Friday, and it still says EUR 2.1 billion. The embargo lifts at 10:00 CET on Thursday 26 November.

Please speak to Hanna as early as possible on Tuesday. Ask her to prepare a corrected replacement and circulate it to the same list once it is signed off, making clear that it supersedes Friday’s copy and retaining the Thursday 10:00 CET embargo. Geert knows I am away and can sign off the corrected release if Hanna needs a senior name.

Before Thursday morning, get Hanna’s confirmation that the corrected release has gone out and that no one is working from the old copy alone.

2. Reassign or reschedule the two journalist calls

Hanna had offered two journalists a background call with me on Wednesday afternoon: one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. The calendar holds are Wednesday 25 November at 14:00 and 15:00, by phone, 20 minutes each, with Hanna still to confirm.

Please ask Hanna to arrange these with you instead if you can take them. If you cannot, ask her to reschedule rather than leaving the journalists expecting a call from me. They should have the corrected EUR 1.4 billion figure and PDF v7 before speaking to anyone.

3. Confirm the revised running order with Tomás

Tomás has warned us that MEP Katarina Lindqvist now has a vote during Thursday lunchtime and must leave at 13:30. He has asked for two changes:

- The presentation should be 15 minutes rather than 20.
- The panel should start at 12:50.

Lindqvist also wants to take at least two questions herself before she leaves. Please agree with Tomás where those questions fit; they cannot be left until the original 13:40 Q&A slot. Also agree who will moderate and close the event once Lindqvist leaves at 13:30.

The working running order is therefore:

- 12:00: guests at the European Parliament security entrance; light lunch outside the room.
- 12:30: welcome by Lindqvist, five minutes.
- 12:35: your presentation, 15 minutes.
- 12:50: panel with you, Dr Abena Owusu-Mensah remotely and Florian Kessler, moderated by Lindqvist.
- Before 13:30: at least two questions involving Lindqvist, in the format agreed with Tomás.
- 13:30: Lindqvist leaves.
- Afterwards: remaining discussion/Q&A and handover of moderation as agreed.
- 14:00: close, unless Tomás agrees a different arrangement.

The venue is the Altiero Spinelli building, in the room booked by Lindqvist’s office. The deck is currently 14 slides; please run it through as a 15-minute presentation rather than simply speaking faster.

4. Meet the badge deadline on Wednesday

Tomás needs the final names of everyone from our side by Wednesday 25 November at 12:00 at the latest. Without those names, security will not admit them. Please send him the list in good time and check that anyone whose attendance has changed is removed or replaced.

Tomás will collect the badges. Guests still need to be at the security entrance by 12:00 on Thursday.

5. Check the panel logistics

Abena’s remote link is in the calendar invite. It has already been tested successfully and works, but please check the connection again before the room fills if the Parliament setup allows it.

The panel participants are:

- Dr Abena Owusu-Mensah, Accra Trade Policy Centre, remote.
- Florian Kessler, Alliance of European Steel Users.
- You.
- Lindqvist as moderator until she has to leave.

6. Handling Kessler and the questions

Expect Kessler to try to make the discussion about the 80% pass-through assumption. Answer it directly, but do not let him set the tone or turn the whole launch into a debate about that one number.

The lines are:

- The 80% pass-through for downstream steel users is our central case in section 4, not the only case we examined.
- Annex B tests 60% and 40% as well. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%.
- Say that openly, including the weakening at 40%. There is no reason to get defensive, and you know these sensitivity runs inside out because you ran them.
- Acknowledge the concern Kessler raises about smaller manufacturers, whose members report much lower pass-through, and then bring the discussion back to the paper’s findings on CBAM revenues and LDCs.

On resource shuffling, we agree that it is a risk. It is addressed in section 5.2, where we recommend the Commission’s monitoring report. Do not waste time pretending the risk does not exist.

Abena was strong on the LDC side during our call and will probably support those points. Give her room to speak, particularly if Kessler begins to dominate.

If anyone asks about the changed revenue estimate, keep it factual: the earlier figure came from the old run without the free-allocation phase-out; the corrected 2030 figure is EUR 1.4 billion; the conclusion stands, but the headline revenue number changes. And if they ask whose mistake it was, it was mine.

7. After the launch

Lucy Tran from the Halvorsen Foundation will attend with a colleague. For their grant report, she needs two photographs from the event and the attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Please arrange in advance for someone to take the photographs and make sure we keep a reliable attendance count. This does not need to compete with the launch itself on Thursday, but it should not disappear afterwards.

Finally: in Lisbon, at the COP side event, you rescued my panel when the projector died. You are better live than you think. You do not need to imitate me, and you certainly do not need to spend the event feeling that you are standing in for me. Lead it as your launch too.

I am sorry again for the correction and for the timing. I would not be comfortable handing this to many people at such short notice, but with you I am. I trust your judgement completely.

Marieke
